facts.claim: One Tuscan planner reports that a high-quality wedding generally lands between €800 and €1,200 per guest. On that basis, 50 guests sits around €40,000 to €60,000, and 100 guests around €80,000 to €120,000.

facts.claim: Food and drink is the biggest line item at roughly a third of the budget, and destination-standard catering usually costs €150 to €220 per guest.
facts.use_note: Same page tiers: 'Expect €110 to €150 per guest at the lower mid-range, €150 to €220 for a strong destination-wedding standard, €220 to €300 for premium service, and more than €300 for a five-star experience.' Extractor wording; confirm before quoting. EUR.

facts.claim: Venue and ceremony costs run from €10,000 to €50,000 or more by venue type, and many service invoices carry 22% VAT. Florals, design and rentals run €25,000 to €80,000, and entertainment and sound €15,000 to €30,000. Catering and bar (€180 to €310+ a head). Full-service planner 10% to 15% of the total. Contingency about 10% of the total.
facts.use_note: Full text read. Page disclaimer: 'All prices are indicative and based on published rates at the time of writing.' Page says elaborate banquets 'may exceed €450 per person'. EUR.

facts.claim: Venue rental runs €400 to €1,500 or more, while catering is priced at €75 to €160 or more a head. A wedding planner typically costs €3,000 to €5,000 or more, and helps with local Greek paperwork, translators and day-of coordination.
facts.use_note: Page also says florals €1,500 to €12,000+, photography €600 to €3,000+, and that accommodation is a separate part of the budget. Le Ciel capacity 'up to 80 seated guests' is relayed from the venue; check the venue site if used. EUR.

facts.claim: Resort ceremony packages range from about US$1,500 to US$5,000 before tax. Transfers run US$400 to US$820 a person by seaplane and US$100 to US$490 by speedboat. Villa stay, per night US$800 to US$3,000+. Reception, per person from US$250+. Tax and service charge 27% (10% service charge plus 17% GST). Green tax, per person per night US$12.
facts.use_note: Table rows on our Maldives guide. Tax rates are from our page only; an official Maldives Inland Revenue Authority source would make them high confidence. USD.

facts.claim: A classic resort wedding runs FJD $10,000 to $20,000, and luxury weddings FJD $25,000 to $75,000 or more. Each guest beyond the package adds about FJD $130 to $180 or more. Legal fees $90 to $145.
facts.use_note: Page also: 'A package often covers the ceremony site, a basic reception setup and a coordinator.' Legal fee from our page only; Fiji government source not checked. FJD.

facts.claim: Most small weddings in Italy for 15 to 40 guests land between €18,000 and €35,000, and micro weddings of 10 to 20 guests typically run €15,000 to €28,000. Budget €800 to €1,600 per guest for a micro wedding and €500 to €1,200 at 20 to 40.

Lead time: '12 to 18 months is comfortable for a peak-season Saturday ... 6 to 9 months is workable for a weekday or a shoulder-season date.' EUR, excludes VAT.

facts.claim: Medical assistance is usually the highest unexpected cost for Australians overseas. Most countries won't give you free or subsidised care. You, or your insurer, must usually pay full price.
facts.use_note: Last updated 18/08/2026. Same page: 'The Australian Government can't pay your bills.' and 'We expect all Australians travelling overseas to take out appropriate insurance for their trip.' No dollar figure for medical costs on this page.

facts.claim: The average price for a comprehensive policy varies from $100 for travel in the Pacific to over $1700 for travel in Africa.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller, CHOICE travel insurance buying guide: How to save money on travel insurance
facts.use_note: Hosted on smartraveller.gov.au but authored by CHOICE (independent consumer body). Table: Europe $267 to $1335, Asia $112 to $1024, Pacific $78 to $307, Americas $495 to $1630 (cheapest and most expensive average policy per region), based on 230,296 quotes collected in March 2026. AUD implied. Note the page text says '$100 for the Pacific' while the table shows $78 cheapest; quote one or the other, not both. Per-traveller cost of risk, useful for the guest-cost section.

facts.claim: Smartraveller says the right travel insurance is as essential as a passport for overseas travel, for every traveller.
Always read the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) before buying; it sets out inclusions, exclusions, definitions, the claims process and emergency support.

When a service has a major problem, a consumer can choose to: cancel the contract and get a refund. This may not be a full refund, as the consumer needs to pay a reasonable amount for any work done so far and as expected, or keep the contract, but pay a lower price that takes the problem into account.
facts.use_note: Modified 13 Nov 2026. General consumer guarantees for services, not wedding-specific. Applies to Australian suppliers under the ACL; overseas suppliers may not be covered (not confirmed here).

facts.claim: Businesses can't take away a consumer's right to a refund or replacement for faulty products or services. It's illegal for businesses to rely on store policies or terms and conditions which deny these rights. Consumers are not entitled to a repair, replacement or refund under the consumer guarantees if they ... simply changed their mind.
facts.use_note: Key nuance for deposits: a couple who cancels by choice has no consumer-guarantee refund right; their position then depends on the contract terms. Ellipsis marks omitted text.

facts.claim: Under the Australian Consumer Law, businesses must not accept payment for products or services if: they don't intend to supply the product or service; they intend to supply different products or services from those promised; they know, or should know, that they won't be able to supply the products or services by the promised date, or within a reasonable time.
facts.source_name: ACCC, Not receiving products or services that are paid for
facts.use_note: Modified 28 June 2026. Relevant to deposits paid far in advance.

facts.claim: Businesses do not have to give replacement services or refunds under the consumer guarantees if the actions of a third party prevented them from supplying their services. For instance, when businesses were prevented from supplying their services due to government restrictions in response to COVID-19. In this situation, consumers' right to a refund or replacement will generally depend on the terms and conditions of the agreement for supply of the service.
facts.source_name: ACCC, Not receiving products or services that are paid for
facts.use_note: Supports 'read the cancellation and postponement terms before paying a deposit'. Not legal advice; writer should say so.

facts.claim: Catering and food, per person €80 to €300+ (about €4,000 to €15,000). Drinks and open bar, per person €20 to €40+ (about €1,000 to €2,000+). ... Standard local menus sit at the lower end, while imported or luxury resort catering pushes past €250 to €300 a head.
facts.use_note: NEW page, not in earlier packs. Live text read 2026-11-26 via Apify (HTTP 200); published date and og:url not captured (Firecrawl out of credits). Benchmark 50 guests. EUR. Note internal inconsistency: €80 to €300 x 50 is not €4,000 to €15,000 at the top end, and drinks €20 to €40 x 50 is €1,000 to €2,000 only per hour-agnostic; quote the per-person rates only, and flag to Nic. H1 says 'A Real Breakdown' but body is an estimate.

facts.claim: A Mykonos wedding for 50 guests typically costs between €15,000 and over €50,000, before guest accommodation. ... Full-service packages for 50 to 100 guests often range from €25,000 to €100,000 or more.
facts.use_note: Totals with guest count; do not divide. 'Before guest accommodation' implies guest rooms are outside the couple's figure. EUR.

facts.claim: Guests arrive by airport transfer and shuttle, and boat transfers add to this when the venue sits on a beach. We confirm transport pricing with each operator, since it varies by venue. We arrange room blocks and build the schedule around transfer timings, so guests arrive rested and on time. ... Can a welcome event and a farewell brunch be added later? Yes, and we include them in the plan from the start so the total reflects the whole weekend. ... Minimum spend: The least a venue requires you to spend on food and drink.
facts.use_note: Welcome and farewell events counted in the couple's total; glossary definition of minimum spend. Who pays transfers and rooms not stated.

facts.claim: Traditionally, guests pay for their own travel to a destination wedding, and couples pay for the celebration itself. ... The three most common additions are group transfers, a welcome event and accommodation for close family. ... Guests usually cover their own flights and most accommodation, while couples host the celebration.
facts.use_note: Owner page for who-pays (link, summarise, do not duplicate). Live text read 2026-11-26 via Apify (HTTP 200, no redirect); og:url and dates not captured (Firecrawl out of credits). Convention, not data.

facts.claim: Essential: The couple hosts the events only. Considered: Adds group transfers, a welcome dinner and a farewell brunch. Hosted: Adds accommodation for parents and the wedding party. Fully hosted: Adds accommodation for every guest. ... Accommodation is often arranged by the couple and paid for by each guest. A held room block gives guests a defined place to book.
facts.use_note: Hosting levels: core of the 'who pays' section. Page also: 'Taking on more of the travel and accommodation costs may mean inviting fewer guests'. It links 'our guide to wedding cost per guest' (the blocked A$38,252 page); do not follow or quote.

facts.claim: Peak-season airfares ... Minimum hotel stays: Properties in popular destinations may require a minimum number of consecutive nights, particularly during peak periods or special events. Payment deadlines: Accommodation deposits, room blocks and hosted experiences may each have separate payment schedules and cancellation conditions. ... Guests may wish to consider travel insurance.
facts.use_note: Guest costs to flag early. Pair travel-insurance line with Smartraveller F-21 to F-24.

facts.claim: Bali charges international visitors IDR 150,000 per person, according to the provincial government's Love Bali platform. In the Maldives, the Inland Revenue Authority sets GST at 17 percent and a Green Tax of US$12 per person per day, reduced to US$6 at hotels on small inhabited islands. ... Calculate them against the number of guests and nights involved, and establish whether guests will pay individually or whether the costs will form part of your accommodation arrangements.
facts.use_note: Live text read 2026-11-26 via Apify (HTTP 200). Per-person levies. 'per person per day' CONFLICTS with Maldives page 'per person per night' (SITE-CONFLICT-05): record both, not resolved here. Official MIRA and Love Bali pages not opened in this pass (see needs).

facts.claim: Le Ciel, for example, requires at least 20 guests over the age of 10 between 20 May and 30 September. Couples who fall below this number are charged an additional €190 for each missing guest. In Dubai and Abu Dhabi, Gulf News reports minimum spends ranging from AED 40,000 for a garden space to AED 120,000 for an outdoor amphitheatre. When reviewing a proposal, look beyond the advertised per-person rate.
facts.use_note: Best guest-minimum example on our site (why small lists cost more per head). Le Ciel is a venue (its terms relayed; venue page not opened). AED 40,000 low end differs from Dubai page low end AED 60,000 (SITE-CONFLICT-06, different venues in scope). EUR/AED.

facts.claim: AION lists welcome drinks from €20 per person per hour, open bar concepts between €25 and €45 per person per hour, and an additional €15 per person for each extra hour. ... At Le Ciel, drinks packages are compulsory for all guests during the ceremony cocktail hour and two-hour dinner. ... At Le Ciel, a gratuity of 7 percent of the food and beverage total is expected and must be paid in cash at the pre-wedding meeting.
facts.use_note: Santorini venues. EUR. Do not use the Vogue US tipping line (US market).

facts.claim: Le Ciel requires couples to arrange guest transfers, making transport another consideration when assessing the venue's overall cost and location.
facts.use_note: Example of a venue making transfers the couple's responsibility. Page also links an older 'who pays for what' guide (brief says do not link that one).

facts.claim: The structure is always the same: a base fee plus a per person rate, wrapped around a guest minimum. ... Compare on true per-guest cost: (package price + mandatory extras + everything the package excludes) divided by your real guest count. ... below the guest minimum you pay for seats nobody fills; far above it, you may unlock the next tier's inclusions for less than the extras would cost individually.
facts.use_note: Canonical URL (per strategist; /all-inclusive-wedding-cost serves the same page). Live text read 2026-11-26 via Apify; page shows 'Published 11 Aug 2026 · Updated 30 Sept 2026'. Method only, no figure. Its dollar figures come from The Knot, DestinationWeddings.com and Zola (blocked) and its FAQ contains conversions: DO NOT USE any figure from this page.

facts.claim: Resort package ... Guest cost profile: Guests pay their own all-inclusive stay; their room nights may subsidise your package. Venue package ... Guests book their own accommodation separately at any price point. ... Guest travel. Never in the package; always in your communication plan. ... The days around the day. Welcome events, recovery brunches and rehearsal dinners are add-ons almost everywhere.
facts.use_note: Who pays for guest stays under resort vs venue packages; welcome events are add-ons. No figures.

facts.claim: Earlier research from the same Florence institute found that food and beverage accounted for 35% of spend, the venue 21%, hospitality 17% and ancillary services 27%.
facts.use_note: The only percentage split by line on our live pages found so far. Italy only, attributed on the page to Florence's Centro Studi Turistici ('earlier research', year not stated). Quote exactly with that attribution; do not generalise to all destinations. Same page also says 'Food and drink is the biggest line item at roughly a third of the budget' (see F-02).

facts.claim: Planner and Entertainment: Planner fees start from around €2,000 to €8,000 and rise with full-service planning. A DJ runs about €500 to €1,200, while a live band can reach €10,000 for one evening.
facts.use_note: Planner fee wording (Italy). EUR. Not our own fee.

facts.claim: Legal Fees: Town hall fees for a civil ceremony vary by comune, typically ranging from €100 to €2,000 and averaging about €500, and paperwork in Italy and your home country adds roughly €600. Your Wedded Advisor coordinates the paperwork with celebrants and lawyers on the ground.
facts.use_note: Cost line only. Not a legal-process source; legal process must come from an official authority.

facts.claim: Lake Como: ... A ceremony at Villa del Balbianello for up to 50 guests, held while the villa is closed to the public, is quoted at about €6,900, and 22% VAT applies to each FAI invoice line. June and September dates are often gone 18 months ahead. ... Tuscany: ... Exclusive hire for 60 to 80 guests across three nights typically starts at around €27,000 to €30,000 in 2026. Because the borgo doubles as accommodation, it can replace a separate hotel block. Amalfi Coast: ... Guests are usually moved by boat ... Budget for water transfers from the start.
facts.use_note: Venue, accommodation and transfer lines (Italy). Tuscany overlaps F-58.

facts.claim: Move Your Date: At one Lake Garda villa, the same package costs €24,000 in March, April and October but €30,000 in July and August. ... Marry Legally at Home: Some couples complete the legal marriage at home and hold the ceremony abroad, which removes Italian town hall fees and paperwork. ... Choosing a shoulder-season month can take up to a fifth off your venue fee.
facts.use_note: 'up to a fifth' is the page's own wording; do not restate as a percentage.

facts.claim: Track every line as you go with the free budget tool in Wonderland Studio.
facts.use_note: Live wording of what the budget tool does: track every line. Contains the word 'free', which is a price/plan term: per brief, do not repeat 'free' unless Nic confirms. Use 'track every line' only.

facts.claim: Before transferring a deposit, review the payment schedule, cancellation policy, refund conditions and accepted currencies. If paying internationally, compare the costs of bank transfers and card payments rather than assuming the quoted amount is the amount that will leave your account.
facts.use_note: Our own currency and payment advice. Section 10 'Card Fees, Payment Terms and Non-Refundable Deposits'.

facts.claim: Payment methods can carry their own costs, too. Experian reports that card issuers typically charge foreign transaction fees of 1 to 3 percent, potentially alongside a currency conversion markup.
facts.use_note: Figure relayed from Experian (credit bureau, likely US context), not an Australian official source. Not a competitor, but cite only as 'our hidden-costs guide notes'; prefer the Moneysmart line if found.

facts.claim: Le Ciel requires a 50 percent deposit of €2,100, with the remaining venue fee due 365 days before the wedding. Payments are non-refundable, and the venue accepts bank transfers only.
facts.use_note: Venue example of deposit terms (Santorini).

facts.claim: Le Ciel requires a professional planner for table decoration, flowers, cake, entertainers and legal paperwork. It also prohibits outside DJs. ... At Le Ciel, a gratuity of 7 percent of the food and beverage total is expected and must be paid in cash at the pre-wedding meeting.
facts.use_note: Planner, florals, entertainment and tipping lines (one venue). Vogue tipping figures on same page are US, not quoted here.

facts.claim: Wedded Wonderland reviews these details with couples, examining proposals line by line to establish what is included, excluded or yet to be confirmed. ... A destination wedding budget should reflect the cost of delivering the entire celebration, not simply the venue's opening quote.
facts.use_note: Our own line-by-line method wording; fits the article angle.

facts.claim: Calculate them against the number of guests and nights involved, and establish whether guests will pay individually or whether the costs will form part of your accommodation arrangements.
facts.use_note: Levies line advice. Green tax wording conflict stays open (SITE-CONFLICT-05).

facts.claim: Venue and catering. At home, you hire a venue and a caterer separately. Many resorts abroad sell packages that bundle the venue, food, drinks and a coordinator, priced by guest count. ... Vendors. Using local photographers, florists and hair and makeup teams saves paying for anyone's travel. Flying your favorite vendors in adds their flights and time. Decor. A beach, a vineyard or a villa garden already looks the part, so many couples spend less on styling. Travel and the honeymoon. You pay for your own trip, but the wedding and the honeymoon can be the same trip. Paperwork. A legal wedding abroad can mean translated, certified documents. ... Planning help. Planning from another country is harder, which is where a planner or the resort's coordinator earns their fee.
facts.use_note: Line-by-line differences, no figures. US spelling ('favorite') on page; writer to use AU spelling in own prose.

facts.claim: Budget separately for your own travel and any guest events, such as a welcome dinner. ... Some couples also host a welcome dinner or a group activity during the trip, which goes on the couple's budget.
facts.use_note: Welcome and farewell events line. No cost figure (G-03 still open).

facts.claim: Venue hire, per day €3,000 to €20,000+; Catering, per person €150 to €250+; Wedding planner €3,000 to €7,000+; Photography and video €2,000 to €8,000+; Single-day wedding, 50 guests About €35,000 to €45,000; Multi-day wedding, 50 guests €50,000 to €75,000+; Luxury wedding €80,000 to €150,000+; Overall total for 50 guests €35,000 to €75,000+
facts.use_note: Tuscany, 50 guests, table 'Range (EUR)'. Page H1 is 'Wedding in Italy Cost for 50 Guests in Tuscany' under Real Weddings but body is indicative estimates, no named couple: do not call it a real wedding (see LABEL-ISSUE). Page disclaimer: 'All prices are indicative and based on published rates at the time of writing.' Planner range €3,000 to €7,000+ differs from Italy expert-advice page €2,000 to €8,000 (SITE-CONFLICT-09).

facts.claim: Venue hire and catering carry most of the total, followed by the planner and photography and video.
facts.use_note: Ranking of lines without percentages. Do not add percentages.

facts.claim: It is important to distinguish between venue hire and minimum-spend requirements, as the latter may contribute towards the catering budget rather than represent an additional fee. ... It works as a floor on catering and bar, so it overlaps with those lines.
facts.use_note: Venue line advice: avoid double counting minimum spend.

facts.claim: The wedding dinner is only one part of the catering budget. A welcome aperitivo, pre-ceremony refreshments and a farewell lunch can introduce additional per-person costs, particularly when drinks, staffing and venue access are included. We account for these occasions alongside the reception when establishing the catering allowance.
facts.use_note: Welcome and farewell events line, no figure.

facts.claim: For a 50-person celebration, the floral and styling budget often centres on the ceremony arrangement, reception tables, personal flowers and selected architectural details. Lighting becomes particularly important for evening celebrations ... Established destination wedding specialists may also charge additional travel, accommodation and transfer expenses when travelling from outside the region. ... Hair and makeup services, including bridal styling and additional appointments for the wedding party, should be scheduled around photography coverage ...
facts.use_note: Florals, photography travel and beauty lines. No floral figure on page.

facts.claim: Government fees, document legalisation, translations and municipal charges should be budgeted separately from the wedding costs outlined above. ... For a celebration of 50 guests, transport between accommodation and the wedding venue should be factored into the budget.
facts.use_note: Legal and transfers lines as budget items. Legal process itself (Nulla Osta, Atto Notorio) must be confirmed by official source (Australian Embassy Rome / DFAT / comune), not this page.

facts.claim: Know where every dollar goes. Set a budget, log deposits and see what is left in every category. ... Every couple gets the full planning suite (website builder with RSVP, guest list, budget tracker, timeline, task list, seating, menu, calendar, decor moodboard and vendor management) ...
facts.use_note: Exact live wording of what the budget tool does. Price, plan and trial wording on the page deliberately not recorded.

facts.claim: When a venue or vendor sends you an invoice or a payment link, you pay it securely through Wedded Wonderland, and your payments sit in your planning hub beside the rest of your plans. ... Deposits, balances and bookings sit together under Payments in your planning hub, so you can see who you have paid and when. ... paying does not by itself confirm a booking.
facts.use_note: Deposit tracking wording. Surcharge wording on page omitted (price term). Nic to confirm whether to mention payments in this article.

facts.claim: If the charge is in a currency other than your card's, your bank or card provider may add its own foreign-transaction charge.
facts.use_note: Our own currency wording (Studio payments FAQ).

facts.claim: How should we split a budget for 120 guests? Most couples put 45 to 50% into venue and catering, then about 10% each on photography and attire. I can set that up in your budget.
facts.use_note: DO NOT CITE without Nic. This is a sample AI Planning Assistant answer in a product demo, not editorial guidance, and no source is given. The demo budget tile on the same page shows 'Venue & catering 42%, Photography 20%, Florals & styling 12%, Attire 35%' (illustrative UI, sums past 100%). Conflicts with B-01. See SITE-CONFLICT-10.

facts.claim: Look for a good currency exchange rate and check the fees when sending money overseas. ... Providers choose the exchange rate they use. They also charge fees. The costs depend on: how much money you send; where you send it; how you send it.
facts.use_note: Official line for paying overseas suppliers in foreign currency. Link at the claim.

facts.claim: It's a good idea to shop around before you send money overseas. Different companies can charge very different prices. You can save money by comparing exchange rates and fees. ... Compare these features: Currency exchange rate: how much your money is worth in another country (for example, how many Australian dollars it takes to buy 1 euro); whether the advertised rate is the rate you get. Exchange rate guarantee: whether the exchange rate stays the same or can change. Transfer fees and commission: the type of conversion fee (a flat rate or a percentage, or both); whether the receiver pays any fees; the 'margin' fee to convert your currency.
facts.use_note: Supports currency buffer line. Moneysmart gives no buffer percentage; do not invent one.

facts.claim: Transfer time: how long the money takes to arrive (it could be instant, take a few minutes, or take up to five business days). ... In Australia, money transfer services must be registered with AUSTRAC (Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre). Before you use a money transfer business, check that it is registered.
facts.use_note: Deposit timing and provider check.

facts.claim: If there's a problem with your transfer, contact the bank or money transfer business first. If you're not happy with their response, and they are a member of the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA), you can complain to AFCA. Beware of scams: If you send money to someone and that person turns out to be a scammer, it's almost impossible to get your money back. Be very careful who you send your money to.
facts.use_note: Pairs with ACCC deposit facts F-25 to F-28.

facts.claim: You cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law.
facts.quote: You cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia.
